primary_sources.supports: File security descriptors and parent ACL inheritance; directory descriptor alone does not control existing child access.
Explicit creation security and SE_DACL_PROTECTED to prevent ACE inheritance.
CreateFile ignores creation security descriptor when opening an existing file.
Security requires a supporting filesystem; creation/open semantics differ.
WAL and SHM files are separate paths; WAL forms part of persistent database state.

finding_scope: Source-based Windows portability/acceptance assessment. Current Open rejects Windows files before SQLite initialization. No actual Windows execution, disclosure, authorization bypass or exploit was demonstrated.

contract_determination.privacy_invariant: Private regular database; new files 0600; unsafe existing files rejected; private backup/restore.
missing_platform_details: Execution identity/SID and permitted additional ACE principals
Private directory and inherited sidecar ACL requirements
Existing database and sidecar rejection versus remediation
Backup/restore ACL semantics and native acceptance
Supported filesystem and path/handle protection boundaries
contract_determination.conclusion: A narrow platform-contract extension and native acceptance are required before claiming Windows support. A conservative single execution-identity profile is technically actionable without choosing new network governance, message-retention or E2EE policy; it should be explicitly adopted and reviewed as a separate patch.

concrete_source_observations.detail: os.OpenFile(...,0600), regular-file check and mode &0077 rejection occur before sql.Open; PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL creates a sidecar obligation.
Regular-file permission bits are synthesized as 0666 or 0444, so the current POSIX mask rejects both.
On Windows only owner-writable bit affects the read-only attribute; other permission bits do not set a DACL.
CreateFileW/A call passes a zero security-attributes pointer; main/journal/WAL creation uses default security.
SHM-file CreateFileW/A call also passes a zero security-attributes pointer.
VACUUM INTO snapshot followed by os.Chmod(0600) is a valid POSIX fixture but does not establish Windows backup ACL privacy.

minimal_proposed_profile: Preserve POSIX behavior in a non-Windows helper. Add a separate Windows helper, with no changes to authorization, SQL schema, retention, message format or driver version.

Document one execution identity as the standalone storage owner; recommend the process-token user SID with a protected owner-only DACL and no implicit broader read/write grants. Any service/group/SYSTEM/Administrators exception must be explicit, not guessed.

Use an explicitly private directory with inheritable owner-only child ACLs so SQLite-created WAL/SHM inherit privacy. Do not silently alter an arbitrary caller directory; require/provision a dedicated directory through an explicit helper or documented setup.

Create a new database with its restrictive security descriptor atomically; validate owner/DACL/regular-file identity through handles for existing DB and sidecars before SQLite writes. Reject missing/null/permissive or unsupported ACL forms without silently chmodding existing data.
Protect the path namespace against check/use replacement, including link/reparse cases; inspect an ACL-supporting filesystem and fail closed when privacy cannot be established.
Use the same documented ACL setup/validation for backup destinations and restore; do not treat Chmod(0600) as ACL validation. Preserve actual SQLite backup/reopen tests.
Reuse pinned golang.org/x/sys/windows v0.48.0 APIs; direct import would require an explicit directness declaration and matching module-boundary guard update, with no version replacement.
required_meaningful_tests: Native fail-before reproduction of current Open rejecting a legitimate private Windows fixture; then fresh-file create/migrate/write/read/close/reopen with the unchanged real driver.
Inspect actual resulting owner and DACL on DB, live WAL and SHM after writes under an inheritable private-directory fixture.

Reject Everyone/Users/Authenticated Users or unrelated SID access, null/missing DACL, unsafe inherited grants, foreign ownership and unsupported ACE forms; confirm rejection preserves existing bytes and ACLs.
Reject unsafe directories, relevant reparse/path replacement cases and unsupported security capability; exercise atomic creation collisions without truncating existing data.
Run actual VACUUM INTO backup/restore with Windows ACL preparation/validation, and verify message/own-view restoration plus private backup and sidecars.

Where a Windows harness can safely provide a second unprivileged token, prove the selected owner can read/write and that other ordinary principals cannot; descriptor parsing alone is not a substitute for native behavior.
Run complete current Windows ordinary suite and Linux/macOS regression/race gates without skips or replacing constructor tests with the borrowed-pool path.
not_sufficient: Treating os.Chmod(0600) as a Windows ACL
Restricting only the main SQLite file while ignoring actual sidecar/backup security
Changing tests to call NewStore only to avoid the standalone constructor
Claiming native success from source inspection or cross-compilation
